studyData.intro: An interrupted arm, a torn-looking field and a needle threaded through the title turn fragmentation into visible form. This is a Nabu reissue catalogued 2022 by a distributor; its actual printing and design date are unverified, and it is not presented as the 2013 first-edition cover.

regions.label: Interrupted red arm
regions.summary: An isolated limb enters from the upper left.

sections.heading: An outlined fragment
sections.body: A red arm and hand extend into the pale field, with open spaces between the fingers and many thin internal marks. The arm is interrupted by the edge rather than joined to a visible full body, making the fragment immediately legible.

sections.heading: A visual opening into fragmentation
sections.body: The separated limb can suggest parts of a body before the title is read. That association is strengthened by the needle and thread below, but the cover does not show a complete creature whose hidden anatomy could be reconstructed.

regions.question: How does an outlined hand feel different from a solid red silhouette?

regions.label: Small English title
regions.summary: A second language offers another entrance.

sections.heading: English in a compact block
sections.body: The English wording gives Ahmed Saadawi and Frankenstein in Baghdad in a small left-aligned block. Green dominates, with a red initial drawing attention to the start of the title. It is much smaller than the Arabic title below.

sections.heading: Two scales of naming
sections.body: The English block can be read quickly as a compact group, while the Arabic title occupies a much wider and heavier area. Their unequal sizes create hierarchy without requiring both languages to use the same line arrangement.

regions.question: How does the red initial help organize the otherwise green English block?

regions.label: Arabic author name
regions.summary: A dark line sits immediately above the title.

sections.heading: Ahmed Saadawi
sections.body: أحمد سعداوي names the author in Arabic. Its smaller scale distinguishes authorship from the broad title below. The dots and other letter marks belong to the name and should not be removed as incidental specks in a close reading.

sections.heading: Separation through size and position
sections.body: The author line is dark like the title but occupies a shallower band. Its position above the framed title keeps the two roles connected, while the surrounding pale space prevents them from becoming a single undifferentiated block.

regions.question: What would make the author and title harder to distinguish if they shared the same size?

regions.label: Large Arabic title
regions.summary: Heavy letters establish the central statement.

sections.heading: Frankenstein in Baghdad
sections.body: The Arabic title reads فرانكشتاين في بغداد. Its broad black letterforms carry much more visual weight than the smaller English block. The words name both the Frankenstein reference and Baghdad, without requiring an English translation to dominate the cover.

sections.heading: Weight inside a thin frame
sections.body: The title’s thick strokes contrast with the very fine reddish rectangular outline around it. This difference keeps the words forceful while the frame remains a light organizing device rather than a heavy competing box.

regions.question: Which is more important to the title’s prominence: thick strokes, large scale or the surrounding pale area?

regions.label: Baghdad on the lower line
regions.kicker: A NAMED PLACE, NOT A GUESSED SKYLINE
regions.summary: The place name gives the title a second step.

sections.heading: A named place, not a guessed skyline
sections.body: في بغداد means “in Baghdad.” The wording supplies the place explicitly, while the city silhouette beneath remains a stylized collection of shapes rather than a reliably identified set of individual buildings.

sections.heading: Words and image reinforce a setting
sections.body: The place wording and the urban silhouette can support one another: one names a city, the other gives the lower cover an urban appearance. That relationship does not make every pictured dome or tower a documented Baghdad landmark.

regions.question: What can the words establish that the silhouette alone cannot?

regions.label: Tall needle and hook
regions.summary: A narrow object rises through the verbal area.

sections.heading: A continuous thin form
sections.body: A tall black needle-like form extends upward from the title, with a curved hook or eye at its top. Its slender vertical differs from the broad Arabic strokes, making it visible even though both use dark ink.

sections.heading: Joining becomes a graphic action
sections.body: Set beside the interrupted arm and red thread, the needle can suggest sewing or joining fragments. This is a visible association between objects and marks; it is not a claim that the title letters themselves document a literal scene.

regions.question: How would the idea of joining change if the needle disappeared but the red thread remained?

regions.label: Red thread and title frame
regions.kicker: A THIN LINE WITH CHANGING DIRECTION
regions.summary: Fine warm lines cross heavier black forms.

sections.heading: A thin line with changing direction
sections.body: Red curves travel around the upper title area and relate to the needle, while a fine reddish frame encloses the wording. Their narrow strokes contrast with the much heavier black letters and recall the outlined red arm above.

sections.heading: A repeated colour of connection
sections.body: The red reappears in the arm, title detail and small labels. Its repetition links otherwise separate parts of the cover, while the line’s curves introduce a sense of continuity among fragmented or interrupted forms.

regions.question: Where does red connect two areas that are far apart on the page?

regions.label: Layered city silhouette
regions.summary: An urban band establishes the lower boundary.

sections.heading: Uneven rooflines and towers
sections.body: The skyline contains low roofs, slender towers and rounded forms in several dark blue-green tones. Their changing heights create an irregular upper boundary, while overlap suggests more than one row of buildings.

sections.heading: No landmark inventory is claimed
sections.body: The cover names Baghdad, but the reproduced silhouette is too stylized to identify each building securely. The study therefore describes towers, roofs and layered shapes without attaching unsupported landmark names or architectural dates.

regions.question: Which forms make this read as a city even when individual buildings remain unnamed?

regions.label: Small lower award lines
regions.summary: Several fine lines add credentials beneath the city.

sections.heading: A quieter band of wording
sections.body: Small pale lines occupy the dark lower area, creating a different reading scale from the large title. Their spacing turns them into a compact group, but some fine wording remains limited by the reproduction’s size.

sections.heading: Credentials without invented detail
sections.body: The lower wording visibly presents recognition and award information. Rather than guessing every tiny line or converting it into a complete prize history, this reading notes its role as supporting endorsement beneath the book’s main identity.

regions.question: Why might an award statement be placed below the city instead of beside the main title?

regions.label: Small upper labels
regions.summary: Compact text occupies the otherwise pale upper right.

sections.heading: A small counterweight
sections.body: Several short dark and red lines sit opposite the interrupted arm, with a narrow red strip at the edge. Their small scale keeps them secondary while preventing the upper-right corner from remaining entirely empty.

sections.heading: Information at the periphery
sections.body: These compact labels provide a closer-reading area around the cover’s main image and title. Their placement at the edge allows the large central wording to dominate while still making room for genre or edition-related information.

regions.question: Does the red edge strip help you notice the small wording, or mainly frame the page?

regions.label: Nabu mark at the foot
regions.summary: A compact publisher mark closes the cover.

sections.heading: A bright lower signature
sections.body: A small red-and-pale Nabu mark sits near the bottom, interrupting the darker lower area. Its compact shape and position distinguish it from both the city silhouette and the longer award lines above.

sections.heading: Publisher and distributor are separate
sections.body: Dar Roueya’s page is the distributor source for this Nabu cover and its catalogued 2022 date. Institutional evidence places Nabu in Baghdad; that supports Iraqi publishing context, not the physical printing location or an independently verified design year.

regions.question: Why is a distributor’s catalogue date weaker evidence for a design date than a dated publisher production record?

regions.label: Torn-looking pale field
regions.kicker: A SURFACE WITH A BROKEN EDGE
regions.summary: An irregular diagonal interrupts the background.

sections.heading: A surface with a broken edge
sections.body: The pale background changes tone across an irregular diagonal, giving the appearance of layered or torn paper. It remains quiet enough to support the dark lettering, while its uneven edge adds another kind of fragmentation to the composition.

sections.heading: A qualified reissue identification
sections.body: The shown Nabu object is catalogued 2022 by Dar Roueya; other retail listings differ, and the actual printing and design dates remain unverified. The conflicting retail ISBN is omitted. The work’s original 2013 publication is a separate fact.

regions.question: How does the torn-looking field relate to the isolated arm without depicting the same kind of fragment?
